messages:
maria: Hey design — need a fresh visualization for our benchmark narrative. goal: one modular diagram that shows latency vs cost tradeoffs across three deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private) + callouts for batching and quantization. want it to be responsive for: webinar slide (1600x900), blog hero (1200x600), and a square social card (1080x1080).

alex: Nice. Do we have the final numbers to plot or should we mock?

maria: I can provide sample CSV. Use these rows as the primary curves, do not hardcode axis labels — make them editable in the figma. also we need an accessible color palette and a mono-outline style for annotations so it prints well.

maria: CSV sample (please use exact values for the prototype):

```
mode,median_latency_ms,unit_cost_cents
hosted,45,0.08
dedicated,28,0.15
private,60,0.12
```

alex: Got it. Designer notes: would you prefer line chart with shaded cost bands or dual-axis? dual-axis can be confusing in social thumbnails.

maria: prefer single primary y-axis for latency and encode cost as stroke weight or a secondary subtle sparkline inset. keep it simple for social. on webinar slide we can add a small table.

emily: Also include a small micro-legend that maps: batching -> left shift in latency, quantization -> cost drop. We might animate the dots for the webinar.

alex: Understood. Deliverables checklist I'm expecting:
- Figma master file with components (chart, legend, callouts)
- SVG export variants for 1600x900, 1200x600, 1080x1080
- PNG exports for social and blog hero
- A short redlines doc with accessibility notes (contrast ratios + font fallback)

sam: timeline?

maria: 1st draft by EOD Thu (1998801248), final by Mon next week. Legal needs to review any comparative claims; leave a placeholder text layer that reads: "internal benchmark results, subject to legal review".

alex: Quick Q for brand: which font stack to use — are we fully on Redwood variable font or use fallback?

emily: Use Redwood Sans variable for headlines, system-ui fallback for bodies. Provide a CSS snippet inside the figma notes.

alex: Will create initial mock and post link. also need to confirm color palette tokens — can someone paste the hexes?

maria: brand colors (final): #1F3BFF (brand-blue), #00B37E (accent-green), #101316 (ink). For accessibility swap: use #0B2A99 for high-contrast blue.

design-bot: Checklist reminder: attach source data, include alt text for images, verify 4.5:1 contrast for body text, run export QA for 2x and 3x. :white_check_mark: 

alex: Mock uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/bench-visuals-proto — contains components + artboards. Notes in the left panel.

maria: Perfect. One more ask: please keep the diagram modular so the product marketing team can swap in different numbers later (text layers and shapes must be native, not flattened).

alex: Yep — everything as editable components. I'll ping when draft is ready.

sam: Thanks team — I'll schedule a 15m review on Fri if we have drafts. :calendar:
